title: Global synchronization of topological signals with time-delayed interactions
authors: Wilfried Segnou, Thierry Njougouo, Diego Garlaschelli, Timoteo Carletti
abstract: Topological signals are dynamical variables supported on higher-order structures such as simplicial or cell complexes. In this work, we investigate the impact of time-delayed interactions on the emergence of global synchronization of topological oscillators, with application to the Stuart-Landau system. We first examine the case where signals are supported on simplexes, or cells, of a given dimension and coupled through the Hodge-Laplace matrix. We derive the Master Stability Function and we prove that for suitable discrete delay values, the stability of the synchronous solution becomes analytically tractable and can be solved by using the Lambert W-function. This analysis yields explicit spectral conditions for Global Topological Synchronization to emerge and shows that admissible delays may either promote or suppress synchronization. We then study delayed interactions between signals supported on simplexes, or cells, of different dimensions coupled by the Dirac operator. Under analogous admissible time delays the variational problem, still related to the Master Stability Function, can again be simplified, however in this case we prove that Global Topological Dirac Synchronization cannot emerge. Numerical simulations on simplicial and cell complexes corroborate and complement these findings.
summary: This work analyzes global synchronization in topological oscillators defined on complexes, incorporating the effects of time delays. It distinguishes between coupling via the Hodge-Laplace matrix and the Dirac operator, finding that delays can promote synchronization in one case but prevent it in the other. The findings highlight the critical role of coupling structure and delay time in determining the stability of collective states.
main_problem: The paper investigates how time-delayed interactions affect the emergence of global synchronization in topological signals defined on higher-order structures like simplicial or cell complexes.
main_result: Global Topological Synchronization (GTS) can emerge for signals coupled via the Hodge-Laplacian with suitable delays, but Global Topological Dirac Synchronization (GTDS) cannot emerge under the same conditions, and delay can both promote and suppress synchronization depending on the coupling operator.
method: The analysis involves deriving the Master Stability Function and solving transcendental characteristic equations using the Lambert W-function for delayed differential equations.
model_or_system: The system models topological signals (dynamical variables) supported on $k$-simplices or $k$-cells, whose time evolution is governed by delayed differential equations coupled via the Hodge-Laplace matrix or the Dirac operator.
key_observables: Global synchronization state (order parameters), dispersion relations, and the time evolution of complex amplitudes.
important_parameters: The time delay ($	au$), the coupling operator (Hodge-Laplace vs. Dirac), and the specific geometry of the complex (e.g., torus).
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes homogeneous delays and relies on exploiting the Hodge or Dirac decomposition to simplify the stability analysis.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the complexes used (e.g., 1-simplicial, 2-cell torus) and show time evolution of order parameters comparing synchronized vs. desynchronized states under delayed vs. non-delayed coupling.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining topological signals, then analyzing delayed interactions for same-dimension signals (Hodge-Laplacian), and finally addressing different-dimension signals (Dirac operator).
why_interesting: The study of synchronization in complex, structured systems using delay dynamics provides a rich theoretical framework applicable to pattern formation and collective behavior in many physical systems, including those modeled by network dynamics.

In both cases, edges orientations are denoted by the arrows drawn on the latter, while the faces by the curved arrows.

FIG. 2: Schematic representation of delayed Hodge interactions and delayed Dirac interactions. Top panels illustrate delayed interactions mediated by the Hodge-Laplacian and the Dirac operator in a simplicial complex, whereas the bottom panels depict the corre- sponding interactions in a cell complex. Simplexes and cells are oriented, with straight arrows on links and curved arrows for 2-simplexes or 2-cells.
